title: Session bundle econ pad — decay budgets & reserve trigger maths
content:
Quick brain dump: session-bundle idea with decaying token budgets + reserve-triggering rules. Rough math + scenarios. Not for prime time — just trying to get intuition for tradeoffs between fixed credits, variable token velocity, and when to force move to reserved commit.

Context / goal:
- Problem: many users generate lots of short chat sessions + occasional long sessions -> unpredictable per-customer unit cost.
- Objective: Offer a compact bundle (e.g., 1000 session-credits / month) that maps to a hybrid of tokens + per-session overhead while limiting extreme tail cost exposure.
- Keep friction low for PLG signup; surface a simple conversion to tokens and to reserved triggers.

High-level model components (inputs):
- avg_gen_cost_per_1k_tokens = $0.35 (model compute only, baseline vv-small model)
- infra + infra-ops overhead per 1k tokens = $0.05 -> combined = $0.40 / 1k tokens = $0.0004 / token
- avg_tokens_per_short_session = 120 tokens (prompt+reply)
- avg_tokens_per-long_session = 2500 tokens (long multi-turn)
- session_fixed_handling_cost (routing, trace, db roundtrip amortized) = $0.002 / session
- cache hit savings: prefix caching reduces tokens served by ~20% on returning users (apply in scenario)

Session-credit design:
- 1 session-credit = covers session_fixed_handling_cost + budgeted token allowance + safety buffer
- Tier idea: Starter bundle = 250 session-credits for $9/mo, Standard = 2,000 credits for $49/mo, Pro = 10,000 credits for $199/mo. (numbers intentionally rough)
- Map credits -> tokens: define nominal_tokens_per_credit = 200 tokens (can be tuned)
- Effective cost per credit (cost to Redwood) = session_fixed_handling_cost + nominal_tokens_per_credit * token_unit_cost
   = $0.002 + 200 * $0.0004 = $0.002 + $0.08 = $0.082 per credit

Why decay budgets?
- Prevent stockpiling/hoarding of credits across many idle sessions. Encourage regular usage while avoiding big one-off long sessions draining bundle.
- Implement linear decay: each credit allocated has an expiry window (e.g., 90 days) and decays by X% per week after inactivity. Simpler: sliding window consumption only counts sessions in last 30 days.

Reserve-triggering rule (hybrid product behavior):
- Monitor customer real-time: If 7-day rolling average credit burn rate exceeds 2.5x the included rate for 2 consecutive weeks, nudge to reserved capacity commit.
- Suggest reserve plans sized to 70% of observed peak sustained rate to avoid over-commit pain.

Examples / back-of-envelope scenarios:
1) Typical PLG starter user (daily chat, mostly short):
   - 30 sessions / month * 120 tokens = 3,600 tokens = ~3.6k -> credits needed = 3,600 / 200 = 18 credits/month
   - Cost to Redwood ~ 18 * $0.082 = $1.48/mo -> margin on $9 pack is healthy but need CAC considerations

2) Power user (50 short sessions + 5 long sessions):
   - Short: 50 * 120 = 6,000 tokens; Long: 5 * 2,500 = 12,500 tokens -> total = 18,500 tokens -> credits = 92.5 -> ~93 credits
   - Cost to Redwood = 93 * $0.082 = $7.63/mo. If on Standard 2k credits for $49, still wide margin. Tail risk if many long sessions.

3) Burst long-session customer (two huge sessions):
   - 2 * 25k token sessions = 50k tokens -> credits = 250 -> cost to Redwood = $20.5
   - If they bought Starter 250-credits for $9, Redwood loses money. Mitigate by:
     * soft caps: sessions > 10k tokens flagged -> billed at pay-as-you-go token rate beyond bundle
     * apply per-session safety buffer: single session cannot consume more than N credits (e.g., 100) unless explicit opt-in

Policy options to avoid losses:
- Hard per-session cap: every session can consume at most 100 credits from a bundle; overflow billed at PAYG rate. (simple, transparent)
- Long-session surcharge: sessions > 5k tokens incur surcharge multiplier 1.5x on token consumption vs short-session tokens.
- Counter-abuse: detect scripted grabs (many small sessions spawning tokens) and throttle / require verification.

SLO-weighted pricing hook (advanced, optional):
- Offer two flavors of bundles: "low-latency" bundles routed to higher-tier nodes (cost +15%); "economy" bundles routed to queued/batched execution (cost -10%). Customers choose based on UX needs.
- Could present as add-on at checkout: +$X/mo for low-latency credits. Operationally map via routing policy and autoscaling pools.

Break-even CAC quick calc (very rough):
- assume CAC = $40 for Starter cohort; ARPU from $9 pack = $9/mo; gross margin per user = (price - cost)/price -> cost to Redwood per user baseline (typical) ~ $1.5/mo -> gross margin ~$7.5/mo -> payback ~ 5.3 months. If CAC > 5 months LTV issues. Need retention > 6 months.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Tune nominal_tokens_per_credit by cohort (conversational vs single-shot embeddings-heavy). Maybe have separate credit types (chat-credit vs embedding-credit) to reduce cross-subsidy.
- Exact decay rule mechanics: time-window approach probably simpler to explain than continuous decay.
- UX language: avoid "decay" words for customers; call it "rolling bundle" or "active-months".
- How to implement per-session caps without hurting usage flow? Add clear opt-in modal when session > X tokens.
- Mapping to reserved capacity sales motion: define clear thresholds + one-click recommend reserve plan from Console.

Notes for engineering feasibility check (send to infra/product infra):
- Need real-time per-session token counter exposed to billing infra -> tie into routing/logging.
- Billing system must support per-session overflow billing and flags for long-session surcharges.
- Console UX: show live burn-rate + projected days-to-runout at current pace.

Random thoughts:
- Could experiment with a tiny free starter bundle with very low per-session caps to stimulate sign-ups but reduce tail risk.
- Consider embedding credits separate because embedding units have wildly different cost profile and velocity.
- Use model-level heuristics to auto-apply 20% token-savings for repeat prompts (detect reuse) and reflect in estimator in Console.

Small checklist before next sync:
- [ ] Run cohort sim with real traffic trace (ask analytics for 30-day sample)
- [ ] Propose three starter price points and compute loss rates for 95th percentile usage
- [ ] Draft UX microcopy for per-session overflow modal
- [ ] Engineering spike: how expensive to track per-session tokens at scale?

End of pad — keep short notes here and convert to more formal doc after simulation results.

-- Ava
